topics.title: Ticket booking (BookMyShow)
topics.description: Ticket booking (BookMyShow) within Classic Case Studies.
keyConcepts: 1. The question as an interviewer asks it
2. Requirements
F1. Browse movies → showtimes → seat map.
F2. Hold seats (temporary lock) with a countdown.
F3. Pay, get a ticket with QR/barcode; cancel with refund rules.
F4. Seat categories (regular, premium, recliner, couple) with different pricing.
F5. Multi-seat booking and multi-person splits.
F6. Showtime cancellation / refunds en masse.
F7. Access control: age ratings, blocked screens, gendered seating (some markets).
F8. Notifications (confirmation, cancellation).
N1. No double booking, ever. This is the absolute constraint.
N2. Seat-map load < 200 ms at peak (a popular show sells out in seconds).

F1. Product catalog: browse, search, facets, variations (size/color), related items.

topics.title: Payment system
topics.description: Payment system within Classic Case Studies.
keyConcepts: 1. The question as an interviewer asks it
2. Requirements
F1. Authorize, capture, void, refund (full and partial), credit.
F2. Multiple providers (Stripe, Adyen, bank acquirer) with failover.
F3. Multiple methods: cards, wallets, bank transfer, BNPL.
F4. Currencies with FX quote, capture, and settlement.
F5. 3DS/SCA step-up, AVS/CVV checks, tokenized cards, network tokens.
F6. Recurring payments, saved payment methods, mandates.
F7. Refunds, partial refunds, chargeback/dispute intake and representation.
F8. Payouts to sellers/merchants.
N1. Never lose money, never double-charge. RPO = 0 on the ledger.
N2. Authorization latency: < 2 s p99 including provider call and 3DS.

```
                     \-> FAILED (provider/technical)
```

```
  created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ

  INDEX (txn_id)
```

topics.title: Search autocomplete
topics.description: Search autocomplete within Classic Case Studies.
keyConcepts: 1. The question as an interviewer asks it
2. Requirements
F1. Suggestions for prefix input: queries, entities, categories, completions.
F2. Typo tolerance ("gogle" → "google").
F3. Trending boost that decays over hours.
F4. Personalization (recent searches, language, locale).
F5. Category/entity icons and types in the response.
F6. Click-through logging to improve ranking.
F7. Suggestion of the full query with highlighted prefix.
N1. < 50 ms p99 end-to-end from keystroke to render.
N2. At 50M DAU and ~6 keystrokes per session → ~3.5M requests/sec peak. This is the dominant number.
N3. Cache hit rate > 90% — at 3.5k QPS per node, this is where the cost is won or lost.

```
-> 200
```

```
-> 202      (batched, sampled; this is the training signal)
POST /suggest/sync    { "recentSearches":["...","..."], "locale":"en-US" }
-> 200
```

```
queries
  query TEXT PRIMARY KEY
  popularity BIGINT          -- exponentially decayed search count
  click_count BIGINT
  intent ENUM(nav, info, transactional)
  locale, country
  first_seen, last_seen
```

```
trends
  query TEXT, hour TIMESTAMPTZ, score DOUBLE PRECISION     -- 1-min buckets for trending
```

```
click_logs            -- append-only, columnar, 30-90 day TTL
  query_prefix, suggestion, position, ts, session_hash, country, device_class
```

```
dictionary_snapshot   -- versioned artifact per locale, published to all shards
  version, locale, generated_at, trie_blob_uri, size_bytes, checksum
```

```
personalization       -- recent searches per user, Redis, TTL 30 days
  recent:{userId} -> LIST(20) of queries
```

```
Browser (debounce 40ms, abort stale, client LRU)
  |
  v
CDN / Edge PoP cache  (key: prefix+locale+tier; TTL 60-300s; hit rate ~70-85%)
  | miss
  v
Suggest Service (2000+ nodes, no shared state, autoscale on QPS)
  |
  +-- in-process compact TRIE over the top ~50M queries   (~1-2 GB, sharded by hash(prefix))
  |      returns candidates for the prefix
  |
  +-- rank:  score = w1*popularity + w2*trending + w3*personalization + w4*prefixAffinity
  |      trending from Redis (1-min buckets), personalization from recent searches
  |
  +-- if < limit candidates -> long-tail search backend (prefix query + top-N by popularity)
  |      this happens for maybe 5% of requests
  |
  +-- return top-k with highlights
  |
Click logs -> Kafka -> popularity/trending jobs -> trie snapshot -> push to all nodes
```

```
score = 0.55*log1p(decayedPopularity)
      + 0.25*log1p(trendScore)            -- 1-min buckets, 6h half-life
      + 0.15*prefixAffinity              -- length & word-boundary match
      + 0.05*personalization             -- recent searches, exact matches boosted
      + 0.05*intentPrior                 -- 'google' is navigational, boost it
```

topics.title: Web crawler
topics.description: Web crawler within Classic Case Studies.
keyConcepts: 1. The question as an interviewer asks it
2. Requirements
F1. Seed URLs, breadth/depth limits, per-domain politeness.
F2. robots.txt fetch, cache, and enforcement including crawl-delay and wildcards.
F3. Content extraction: HTML parse, canonical URL detection, text, links.
F4. Dedupe by content hash and near-duplicate detection.
F5. Sitemap.xml and RSS ingestion as a priority source.
F6. Recrawl policy by content type and observed change rate.
F7. Link graph for authority estimation (PageRank-like).
F8. Per-user custom crawl scopes (a vertical search engine).
N1. Crawl 1 billion URLs/day = ~11,500 QPS, with a large burst factor.
N2. Politeness: never exceed per-domain rates; robots.txt compliance is a hard requirement, not a nicety.

```
                          "maxDepth": 3, "maxPagesPerDomain": 500, "budget": "permalinks" },
                          "refreshPolicy": "weekly", "priority": "normal" }
-> 201 { "jobId": "j_9f3c", "state": "queued" }

POST /frontier/reprioritize  { "domain":"x", "multiplier": 0.2 }   -> throttle
```

```
POST /index/documents   { "url":"https://...", "canonicalUrl":"...", "contentHash":"...",
                          "fetchedAt":"...", "httpStatus":200, "headers":{...},
                          "text":"...", "links":[{"href":"...","rel":"follow|nofollow"}],
                          "depth":2 }
-> 201 { "docId":"d_88f3", "deduped": false }
409 { "error":"duplicate_content", "canonicalDocId":"d_1234" }
```

```
GET /search/index?urlPattern=...      -> index coverage and freshness per URL pattern
GET /robots?host=example.com          -> current cached robots.txt decision
```

```
frontier                        -- priority queue, sharded by host
  url           TEXT
  host          TEXT            -- shard key
  score         DOUBLE PRECISION  -- priority: authority + freshness + depth + type
  depth         INT
  parent_url    TEXT
  discovered_at TIMESTAMPTZ
  next_fetch_at TIMESTAMPTZ      -- politeness and backoff
  state         ENUM(queued, fetched, failed, dead)
  PRIMARY KEY (host, url)
```

```
robots_cache
  host, robots_txt, fetched_at, expires_at, sitemaps[], checksum
```

```
host_state                       -- one row per host; the politeness brain
  host, last_fetch_at, crawl_delay_ms, consecutive_errors, penalty_until,
  pages_fetched_today, total_pages, avg_response_ms, is_blocked
```

```
documents
  doc_id, url, canonical_url, content_hash, simhash, fetched_at,
  http_status, content_type, byte_size, depth, site_id, title
  INDEX (content_hash)
  INDEX (url)
```

```
link_graph                       -- compact adjacency, columnar/LSM, not a row-per-edge SQL table
  from_doc_id BIGINT, to_url_id BIGINT, anchor_text, rel, first_seen
  clustered by from_doc_id; compressed; batch-built into an ANN/authority index
```

```
crawl_errors / fetch_stats       -- for backoff and for search-result quality signals
```

```
crawl_budget
  job_id, pages_fetched, bytes_fetched, max_pages_per_domain, deadline
```

```
Scheduler / Prioritizer (batch + streaming)
   scores frontier entries: authority, freshness expectation, depth, content type, job priority
   emits to Fetch Scheduler
   |
   v
Fetch Scheduler (sharded by host)
   1. robots cache lookup  (miss -> Robots Fetcher, respects its own cache)
   2. host_state check: crawl-delay, penalty_until, daily page budget  -> defer if not allowed
   3. DNS resolution + SSRF guard (no private/loopback/link-local; re-check after resolve)
   4. HTTP GET with conditional headers: If-Modified-Since / If-None-Match
   5. circuit breaker per host
   |
   +--> Fetch Pool (2,300+ workers, async, HTTP/2, connection reuse, gzip/brotli)
   |
   v
Parser / Extractor (HTML parse, canonical link, link classification, robots meta, hreflang)
   |
   +--> Content Store (raw HTML, text)   [immutable, content-addressed]
   +--> Indexer  (dedupe by hash + SimHash, update inverted index, build link graph edges)
   +--> Link Extractor -> Frontier (new URLs, scored, deduplicated by a fast probabilistic filter)
   +--> Change Detector (conditional-request 304 -> update last_fetched only)
   +--> Authority Job (batch PageRank over the link graph)
```

```
score = w1*authority(page)
      + w2*freshnessExpectation(contentType, observedChangeRate)
      + w3*(1/(1+depth))
      + w4*jobPriority
      + w5*novelty(newURLRatioForHost, unseenNeighborhoodBonus)
      - w6*hostPenalty
```

topics.title: Distributed cache
topics.description: Distributed cache within Classic Case Studies.
keyConcepts: 1. The question as an interviewer asks it
2. Requirements
F1. Get/set/setnx/delete/expire/increment with atomic operations.
F2. TTL-based and LRU/LFU eviction.
F3. Namespaces and per-tenant quotas.
F4. Pub/sub for invalidation across processes.
F5. Optional persistence/restartability.
F6. Optional two-tier (memory + local L1).
N1. < 1 ms p99 from within a region; ~1 ms is also the round-trip floor for a network call, so a remote cache is barely better than the database.
N2. Tens of millions to billions of keys. At ~500 B/key, 100M keys = 50 GB per replica.
N3. Availability: the cache is an *optimization*. Its outage must degrade to origin latency, not to an outage.
N4. Memory-bounded and predictable under a key-cardinality explosion.

```
keyspace layout
  {ns}:{key}                          -- hash tags for cluster slot affinity
  ttl                                   -- absolute expiry (ms epoch)
  value                                 -- bytes
  lru_clock (Redis) / access counter (LFU)
  -- counters alongside the value where atomicity matters
```

```
invalidation_log            -- append-only, the correctness backstop
  origin_node, ns, key, epoch, ts
```

```
namespace_config            -- per-namespace policy, versioned
  ns, max_value_bytes, default_ttl_ms, eviction_policy, quota_bytes, compression
```

```
quota / key_counters        -- per-tenant key count and byte usage
```

```

```

```
Client / Service
   L1: in-process cache (Caffeine/caffeine/go-cache), 1-10 GB per node, 20-30% of hot keys
        | miss (~20-40%)
   L2: regional distributed cache (Redis/Valkey cluster, 3 replicas, 8-16 shards)
        | miss (~1-5%)
   Origin: database (sharded)
        on miss -> read origin -> write L2 -> write L1

Invalidation
   Write to origin -> publish invalidation to Redis pub/sub + append to invalidation_log
   -> every node drops the key from L1 (subscription) and the L2 key is deleted or version-mismatched

Three tiers, one rule: each tier is an optimization over the one below it.
```

F1. Metrics: counters, gauges, histograms, summaries, exemplars, tags.

topics.title: Distributed rate limiter
topics.description: Distributed rate limiter within Classic Case Studies.
keyConcepts: 1. The question as an interviewer asks it
2. Requirements
F1. Per-endpoint limits: e.g. POST /api/orders at 10/min/user, GET /api/search at 60/min/user.
F2. Per-tenant, per-IP, per-API-key, per-device limits.
F3. Composite: a request consumes from *all* applicable limiters (user AND IP AND tenant-global).
F4. Dynamic: limits change at runtime without a deploy (tiers, abuse quarantine).
F5. Response contract: 429 + Retry-After + X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset + which rule tripped.
F6. Burst allowance (token bucket) and sustained rate (leaky bucket / sliding window).
N1. Added latency budget: < 1 ms p99 on the hot path. This constraint eliminates whole designs.
N2. Accuracy: ±1 request at the boundary acceptable; never *systematically* over-admit.
N3. Availability: must fail open when unavailable, or the whole API dies with it. A rate limiter that takes down the API is a worse outage.
N4. Scale to millions of keys, tens of thousands of QPS.

topics.title: Chat and messaging
topics.description: Chat and messaging within Classic Case Studies.
keyConcepts: 1. The question as an interviewer asks it
2. Requirements
F1. One-to-one and group conversations (up to ~1,024 members; broadcast channels for larger).
F2. Send text, image, audio, video, document, location, contact, sticker.
F3. Per-conversation message history with pagination in both directions.
F4. Online/typing indicators, last seen.
F5. Delivery receipts (sent / delivered / read) and read counts in groups.
F6. Presence across multiple devices for one user account.
F7. Offline queue: a message sent while offline is delivered when the device reconnects.
F8. Multi-device: new device pulls full history and stays in sync.
F9. End-to-end encryption by default.
F10. Media upload with resumable, chunked transfer.

```
[Global Anycast LB]

   +--> Presence Service: Redis with TTL
   +--> Push Service: FCM/APNs, collapsed per conversation
```

topics.title: YouTube / video streaming
topics.description: YouTube / video streaming within Classic Case Studies.

2. Requirements

topics.title: Netflix
topics.description: Netflix within Classic Case Studies.
keyConcepts: 1. The question as an interviewer asks it
2. Requirements
F1. Browse (rows by genre), search, title detail, "My List", recommendations.

F3. Adaptive bitrate by bandwidth and device capability.

topics.title: Ticket booking
topics.description: Ticket booking within Classic Case Studies.
keyConcepts: 1. The question as an interviewer asks it
2. Requirements
F1. Browse movies → showtimes → seat map.
F2. Hold seats (temporary lock) with a countdown.
F3. Pay, get a ticket with QR/barcode; cancel with refund rules.
F4. Seat categories (regular, premium, recliner, couple) with different pricing.
F5. Multi-seat booking and multi-person splits.
F6. Showtime cancellation / refunds en masse.
F7. Access control: age ratings, blocked screens, gendered seating (some markets).
F8. Notifications (confirmation, cancellation).
N1. No double booking, ever. This is the absolute constraint.
N2. Seat-map load < 200 ms at peak (a popular show sells out in seconds).

topics.title: Search autocomplete / typeahead
topics.description: Search autocomplete / typeahead within Classic Case Studies.
keyConcepts: 1. The question as an interviewer asks it
2. Requirements
F1. Suggestions for prefix input: queries, entities, categories, completions.
F2. Typo tolerance ("gogle" → "google").
F3. Trending boost that decays over hours.
F4. Personalization (recent searches, language, locale).
F5. Category/entity icons and types in the response.
F6. Click-through logging to improve ranking.
F7. Suggestion of the full query with highlighted prefix.
N1. < 50 ms p99 end-to-end from keystroke to render.
N2. At 50M DAU and ~6 keystrokes per session → ~3.5M requests/sec peak. This is the dominant number.
N3. Cache hit rate > 90% — at 3.5k QPS per node, this is where the cost is won or lost.

```
-> 200
```

```
  locale, country
  first_seen, last_seen
```

```
  version, locale, generated_at, trie_blob_uri, size_bytes, checksum
```


```
Browser (debounce 40ms, abort stale, client LRU)
  |
  v
CDN / Edge PoP cache  (key: prefix+locale+tier; TTL 60-300s; hit rate ~70-85%)
  | miss
  v
Suggest Service (2000+ nodes, no shared state, autoscale on QPS)
  |
  +-- in-process compact TRIE over the top ~50M queries   (~1-2 GB, sharded by hash(prefix))
  |      returns candidates for the prefix
  |
  +-- rank:  score = w1*popularity + w2*trending + w3*personalization + w4*prefixAffinity
  |      trending from Redis (1-min buckets), personalization from recent searches
  |
  +-- if < limit candidates -> long-tail search backend (prefix query + top-N by popularity)
  |      this happens for maybe 5% of requests
  |
  +-- return top-k with highlights
  |
Click logs -> Kafka -> popularity/trending jobs -> trie snapshot -> push to all nodes
```

```
score = 0.55*log1p(decayedPopularity)
      + 0.25*log1p(trendScore)            -- 1-min buckets, 6h half-life
      + 0.15*prefixAffinity              -- length & word-boundary match
      + 0.05*personalization             -- recent searches, exact matches boosted
      + 0.05*intentPrior                 -- 'google' is navigational, boost it
```

keyConcepts: 1. The question as an interviewer asks it
2. Requirements
F1. Metrics: counters, gauges, histograms, summaries, exemplars, tags.
F2. Logs: structured, multi-line, searchable, with retention tiers.
F3. Traces: distributed tracing with context propagation.
F4. Dashboards, ad-hoc query, alerting rules with routing.
F5. Cardinality limits and per-tenant quotas.
F6. Retention policies per metric and log stream.
F7. Backfill, rollups, and downsampling.
N1. Ingest 5M metrics/sec and 1M log lines/sec sustained; 10× burst.
N2. Metric write-to-queryable latency: < 60 s for dashboards, < 10 s for alerting.
N3. Log search latency < 5 s over 30 days.
topics.referenceMarkdown:
```
POST /v1/metrics      (protobuf/snappy over HTTP or gRPC)
  MetricPoint[] { name, type COUNTER|GAUGE|HISTOGRAM, value,
                  labels{env,service,instance,route,status}, ts, exemplars[] }

POST /v1/logs         (OTLP/JSON)
  { "resource": {"service.name":"orders","k8s.pod.name":"..."},
    "severity":"ERROR", "body":"...", "traceId":"...", "spanId":"...",
    "ts":"...", "attributes": {...} }

GET /v1/query?metric=...&labels=...&from=&to=&step=      -> series
POST /v1/query_range  (PromQL-like)  -> matrix
POST /v1/search/logs  { query:"level:ERROR service:orders AND msg:\"timeout\"", from,to }
POST /v1/alert/rules  { expr, for, labels, routes[] }
GET  /v1/cardinality?name=...  -> series count by label, with cost estimate
```

```
series (metrics)
  name, labels MAP, label_values_hash, first_seen, last_seen, type
  -- a series is identified by the full label set; the label set is stored once
  samples: (series_hash, ts) -> value    -- columnar, time-partitioned, downsampled
```

```
exemplars
  series_hash, ts, trace_id, span_id      -- ~1% of samples, the metric→trace bridge
```

```
logs (columnar, partitioned by service and day)
  ts, service, severity, body, attributes MAP, trace_id, span_id
  -- inverted index on selected attributes; full-text index on body
```

```
traces (spans)
  trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id, service, name, start_ns, duration_ns,
  attributes, events, status
  -- indexed by trace_id for tree reconstruction
```

```
retention / rollup policy
  metric: raw 15d -> 5m rollup 90d -> 1h rollup 15mo
  log:   full 7d -> sampled-indexed 30d -> cold object storage 90d
```

```
alert_rules  expr, evaluation_interval, for_window, route, mute_windows, runbook_url
```

```
All services (SDK: OTel + Prometheus client)
  metrics --push--> Collector fleet (agent on node, autoscaled, sharded by service)
  logs    --push--> Collector fleet
  traces  --push--> Collector fleet
       |
       v
  Ingest (Kafka as the buffer: durable, replayable, absorbs 10x bursts)
       |
       +--> Metrics path: compaction -> TSDB (time-partitioned, downsampled)
       +--> Logs path:    parse/normalize -> columnar store + index
       |                   -> object storage (cold, cheap)
       +--> Traces:       trace store with tail sampling
       +--> Hot-tier:     last 15 min in Redis/in-memory for dashboards
       |
       v
  Query API (fan-out by tenant/time range) -> Grafana / ad-hoc / alerting
  Alert evaluator -> routing (PagerDuty/Slack) with grouping and suppression

Principle: the emitting service must never block. If the pipeline is unhealthy,
drop or buffer locally and report that it did.
```
